assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a diffuse flux of TeV-PeV astrophysical neutrinos, later tied to the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy as a new observational window. It is the sort of detector-driven discovery I value: a cubic-kilometre instrument built in Antarctic ice, with years of calibration and systematics control behind the claim.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and is the single credited name here. Because a prize needs credit shared across a large collaboration and its predecessors (AMANDA, the DUMAND and Baikal ideas), a one-person configuration is defensible for the instrument vision but may be criticised as incomplete; I only have the supplied name to work with.
assessment.maturity: Strong. The diffuse flux has been seen in several channels (through-going muons, cascades, starting events) and the source associations have grown over the last decade; KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD add some independent confirmation. Timing is good, though identification of the dominant source classes is still open.
uncertainties: Credit among IceCube leaders and precursor experiments is not resolved by the single supplied name.
Origin of the diffuse flux is not settled; only a few source associations are established.
Independent confirmation of the full flux by other large detectors is still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of gamma-ray bursts by BeppoSAX, X-ray and optical afterglows, and redshift measurements settled that bursts are cosmological, one of the great astrophysical puzzles. It is a clean observational result that changed a field and is a textbook example of an instrument (wide-field camera plus fast pointing) making the discovery.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX GRB monitor and narrow-field follow-up that gave the first X-ray afterglow in 1997; Kulkarni led the optical, radio and redshift programme with colleagues at Caltech. The van Paradijs optical identification and the Metzger redshift team are not in the supplied names, so the credit boundary is a real point of contention.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: nearly three decades of confirmation, Swift and Fermi samples, links to supernovae and to neutron-star mergers (GW170817). Recognition is arguably overdue and risks losing deserving people over time.
uncertainties: Van Paradijs (deceased) and others are not in the supplied credit; who is decisive is disputed.
Whether the prize should recognise the X-ray localisation, the optical counterpart or the redshift step.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a nonzero theta13 completed the three-flavour neutrino mixing picture and enabled the search for leptonic CP violation. The Daya Bay result was a precision reactor-antineutrino measurement with identical near and far detectors, an elegant instrument-based design with excellent control of systematics.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay's Wang and Luk led the collaboration and the experiment's design; Nishikawa is credited through T2K's electron-neutrino appearance. Double Chooz and RENO observed it independently, and neither team's leaders are in the supplied names, so the three-person limit makes the configuration awkward. I propose the two Daya Bay leaders since they provided the decisive precision, though T2K deserves discussion.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K. Following the 2015 prize for oscillations, the committee may view this as a follow-on and not a new conceptual step.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will see theta13 as sufficiently distinct from the 2015 oscillation prize.
Allocation between the reactor experiments and T2K, and exclusion of RENO and Double Chooz leaders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, with its flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity, created a tunable platform for strongly correlated matter and a new subfield (moire materials). The theory prediction followed by experiment is a strong narrative of lasting impact. This is outside my own expertise in condensed matter, so I lean on colleagues for the physics details.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat-band magic angle in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Eva Andrei's earlier STM evidence for flat bands is also relevant, and the supplied list allows only three of four names. A theory-plus-experiment trio is natural.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups worldwide; the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, and the field is still moving fast. Reasonably mature as a discovery, early as a full understanding.
uncertainties: Credit for Andrei and others (Dean, Young, Kim and Yacoby-type contributions) falls outside the three-name limit.
Superconducting mechanism remains unsettled, which may argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level use magic-wavelength trapping proposed by Katori to give a new measurement capability, with applications from geodesy to tests of fundamental constants and prospective redefinition of the second. It is a precision-instrument achievement of the kind I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built early Sr clocks; Ye brought it to the highest accuracy and stability at JILA and with the frequency comb. The pair is a coherent proposal; Hall and Hansch were already recognised (2005) for the comb, and Wineland for ion clocks, so some overlap may be argued.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with several independent groups (Japan, JILA, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) at similar accuracy. The redefinition of the second has not yet happened, which does not affect the physical discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes on frequency combs and ion control.
Contribution of other groups (Ludlow, Ushijima, Lemonde) is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing-array evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new GW band and fits supermassive black-hole binaries. As an astroparticle experimentalist I am sympathetic to a new window, but the detection claim is at a statistical level below the discovery threshold used elsewhere.
assessment.attribution: Kramer, McLaughlin and Manchester were leaders of the EPTA, NANOGrav and PPTA respectively; however, the evidence in 2023 was a collaborative effort by hundreds of people, and Hellings-Downs correlations measured jointly by IPTA is the real result. Credit may be better assigned to pulsar timing pioneers than to the current leaders.
assessment.maturity: Premature. Different PTAs agree on a common signal at roughly 3-4 sigma; no individual source and no firm origin. More data from the IPTA, MeerKAT and FAST are needed.
uncertainties: Significance is below 5 sigma and astrophysical versus cosmological origin is unclear.
Credit allocation across three major PTA collaborations is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made superconducting artificial atoms strongly coupled to microwave resonators, the architecture for transmon qubits and dispersive readout and the basis of present quantum processors. Its impact is large, though quantum information is outside my expertise and I defer to colleagues.
assessment.attribution: Blais gave the theoretical proposal (2004), Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first strong-coupling experiments. The trio is balanced between theory and experiment. Overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits (Clarke, Devoret, Martinis) may complicate the case.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely adopted; the key physics is mature. The close temporal link to the 2025 prize could mean that a quantum-circuits prize is not wanted so soon.
uncertainties: Distance from the 2025 prize and whether the committee sees it as a separate discovery.
Credit for Devoret, Nakamura and others involved in the early qubits is not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the SDSS and 2dFGRS galaxy clustering gave a robust standard ruler, central to dark-energy constraints, and is continued by BOSS, eBOSS and DESI. The method is physically clean and rests on well-understood systematics.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein et al. (SDSS LRG) and Cole et al. (2dFGRS) published the first detections in 2005, with Percival leading the later combined analyses. Many survey leaders and theorists (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zeldovich) have claims, so the supplied trio is a narrower credit than the history suggests.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by multiple surveys, but its recognition may be linked to the dark-energy discoveries already honoured in 2011; DESI hints at evolving dark energy are still unresolved.
uncertainties: Credit for the original theory of acoustic peaks is not captured by the names.
Whether the committee sees it as a technique or as a distinct discovery.
